So the rich man will also fade away in his pursuits.17 1812 Blessed19 is a person who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life20 which the Lord21 promised to those who love22 him.23 13 Let no man say when he is tempted, “I am tempted by God24,” for God can’t be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one. 14 But each one is tempted when he is drawn away by his own lust and enticed. 15 Then the lust, when it has conceived, bears sin25. The sin, when it is full grown, produces death. 16 Don’t be deceived, my beloved brothers. 17 Every good gift and every perfect26 gift is from above, coming down from the Father27 of lights, with whom can be no variation nor turning shadow.2829 18 Of his own will he gave birth to us by the word30 of truth31, that we should be a kind of first fruits of his creatures.32 19 So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger; 20 for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness33 of God34. 21 Therefore, putting away all filthiness and overflowing of wickedness, receive with humility the implanted word35, which is able to save36 your souls.37 22 But be doers of the word38, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.39 23 For if anyone is a hearer of the word40 and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror;41 24 for he sees himself, and goes away42, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was.43 25 But he who looks into the perfect44 law of freedom and continues, not being a hearer who forgets but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed45 in what he does.46 26 If anyone among you thinks himself to be religious while he doesn’t bridle his tongue, but deceives his heart47, this man’s religion is worthless.48 27 Pure religion and undefiled before our God49 and Father50 is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos II.13 (c. 350 AD)

'I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty' — Athanasius marks egō eimi to alpha kai to ō (I-AM the alpha and the omega) as the Apocalyptic-Christ's self-predication of divine-comprehension. The alpha-and-omega names the all-encompassing-divine-priority-and-finality (no creature could rightly predicate this of itself). The ho ōn kai ho ēn kai ho erchomenos (the-One-being, the-One-was, the-One-coming) is the Apocalyptic-expansion of the LXX-Ex 3:14 ho ōn — the incarnate-Christ taking-up the burning-bush-self-naming and extending it across the eternal-time-axis. The ho pantokratōr (the-Almighty) is the LXX-translation of Hebrew-El-Shaddai, the highest divine-power-predication. The Tewahedo Apocalyptic-iconology (the Christ-Pantocrator iconography of every Tewahedo-church dome) cites Rev 1:8 as the canonical-self-predication.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). A A lpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet, as Omega is the last. These letters occur in the text of Revelation 1:8,11; 21:6; 22:13, and are represented by “Alpha” and “Omega” respectively (omitted in R.V., 1:11). They mean “the first and last.” (Comp. Hebrews 12:2; Isaiah 41:4; 44:6; Revelation 1:11,17; 2:8.) In the symbols of the early Christian Church these two letters are frequently combined with the cross or with Christ’s monogram to denote his divinity. [Reviewer: condense Easton's entry as needed.]

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). PERGAMOS the chief city of Mysia, in Asia Minor. One of the “seven churches” was planted here (Revelation 1:11; 2:17). It was noted for its wickedness, insomuch that our Lord says “Satan’s seat” was there. The church of Pergamos was rebuked for swerving from the truth and embracing the doctrines of Balaam and the Nicolaitanes. Antipas, Christ’s “faithful martyr,” here sealed his testimony with his blood. This city stood on the banks of the river Caicus, about 20 miles from the sea.… [Reviewer: condense Easton's entry as needed.]

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). THYATIRA a city of Asia Minor, on the borders of Lydia and Mysia. Its modern name is Ak-hissar, i.e., “white castle.” Here was one of the seven churches (Revelation 1:11; 2:18-28). Lydia, the seller of purple, or rather of cloth dyed with this colour, was from this city (Acts 16:14). It was and still is famous for its dyeing. Among the ruins, inscriptions have been found relating to the guild of dyers in that city in ancient times. [Reviewer: condense Easton's entry as needed.]

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §17 (c. 350 AD)

'I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death' — Athanasius marks egō eimi ho zōn, kai egenomēn nekros, kai idou zōn eimi eis tous aiōnas (I-AM the-living-one, and I-became dead, and behold I-AM living unto the ages) as the APOCALYPTIC PASCHAL-IDENTITY-OATH of the risen-Christ. The egō eimi self-predicate identifies the speaker with the Exodus 3:14 divine-Name; the egenomēn nekros (I-BECAME dead) names the assumed-flesh's-genuine-death — the Word becomes-dead via-the-flesh, the divine-impassibility preserved by-becoming-dead-in-the-flesh-only; the zōn eimi eis tous aiōnas names the resurrection-as-eternal-state. The 'keys of Hades and of Death' name the Word's-Paschal-cosmic-victory-authority. Tewahedo Eastern Easter Trisagion-paschal-chant cites Rev 1:18 as the resurrection-Paschal-acclamation.

NICOLAITANES T he church at Ephesus (Revelation 2:6) is commended for hating the “deeds” of the Nicolaitanes, and the church of Pergamos is blamed for having them who hold their “doctrines” (15). ↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Epistulae ad Serapionem 1.28 (c. 350 AD)

'And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come' — Athanasius marks the APOCALYPTIC TRISAGION (hagios hagios hagios kyrios ho theos ho pantokratōr) as the ECHO of Isa 6:3's seraphic-trisagion, now-explicitly-Trinitarian in its three-fold-holy. The trisagion is the heavenly-liturgy the earthly-liturgy joins-with (cf. the Sanctus in every Eucharistic-Anaphora). The three-fold-holy is patristically-read as Trinitarian: holy-Father + holy-Son + holy-Spirit, one-Lord-God-Almighty. Athanasius cites the trisagion in Serapion 1.28 against Tropici-pneumatomachian denial of the Spirit's-divinity: the three-fold-holy positively-includes the Spirit in the divine-glory. Tewahedo Anaphora preserves the trisagion as the canonical eucharistic-Trinitarian acclamation.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §20 (c. 350 AD)

'And they sung a new song, saying, Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation' — Athanasius marks axios ei labein to biblion... hoti esphagēs kai ēgorasas tō theō en tō haimati sou (thou art WORTHY to take the book... for thou wast slain and hast purchased to God by thy blood) as the APOCALYPTIC REDEMPTION-BY-BLOOD anchor. The worthiness (axios) is HYPER-CREATURELY: only the divine-incarnate could redeem the cosmos. The ēgorasas (purchased / redeemed) is commercial-language: the Word's-blood is the redemption-price. The ek pasēs phylēs kai glōssēs (out of every tribe and tongue) marks the cosmic-scope: the redemption is for all-humanity, not Israel-only. Tewahedo Anaphora cites Rev 5:9 at the Communion-distribution as the universal-redemption-by-blood acclamation.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos II.23 (c. 350 AD)

'And every creature which is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them, heard I saying, Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever' — Athanasius marks pan ktisma (every creature) worshiping tō kathēmenō epi tō thronō kai tō arniō (the-One-sitting upon the throne AND the Lamb) as the cosmic-Apocalyptic-divinity confession. The verse explicitly-distinguishes the Lamb (the incarnate-Christ) from pan-ktisma (every-creature) — the Lamb is therefore-NOT among-the-creatures, but stands with the Father-on-the-throne as the joint-recipient of cosmic-creaturely-worship. The four-fold doxology (eulogia + timē + doxa + kratos — blessing + honor + glory + power) is offered indistinguishably to Father-and-Lamb, marking ontological-equality. The Tewahedo Anaphora doxological-section cites Rev 5:13 + 7:10 + 11:15 as the apocalyptic-divinity-triad.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §17 (c. 350 AD)

'That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life' — Athanasius marks the four-fold sensory-witness (akēkoamen + heōrakamen + etheasametha + epsēlaphēsan — heard, seen, beheld, handled) as the Johannine apostolic-anti-Docetic confession. The Word-of-life is NOT a phantasm, NOT a Gnostic-apparition, NOT a Docetic-appearance — he is hearable, visible, examinable, palpable. The four-fold-witness pattern matches the four-canonical-Gospels (eyewitness Mt, hearer-of-Petrine-witness Mk, investigator-Lk, beloved-disciple-Jn) such that the incarnate-Word's sensory-accessibility is canonically-witnessed. The Tewahedo apostolic-succession (Frumentius-through-Athanasius-through-the-Twelve) cites 1 Jn 1:1-3 as the apostolic-eyewitness-warrant.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §54 (c. 350 AD)

'Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is' — Athanasius marks homoioi autō esometha (we-shall-be like-him) as the eschatological-theosis-fulfillment of the Athanasian deification-doctrine. The homoioi-autō is not mere moral-similarity (which any creature could in principle achieve) but the kath'-homoiōsin-theou likeness-to-God that Gen 1:26's creation-blueprint envisioned and that the Fall fragmented and that the Word's-incarnation restores. The hoti opsometha auton kathōs estin (for we shall see him as he is) names the beatific-vision that COMPLETES the theosis: face-to-face vision of the incarnate-divine-Person produces the final-conformity-to-his-image (cf. 2 Cor 3:18 'we all... beholding... are changed into the same image'). The Tewahedo eschatological-hymnody cites 1 Jn 3:2 + 2 Cor 3:18 + Rev 22:4 as the beatific-vision-triad.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §25 (c. 350 AD)

'He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil' — Athanasius marks eis touto ephanerōthē ho Huios tou theou hina lysē ta erga tou diabolou (for THIS purpose was-manifested the Son-of-God, that he might LOOSEN-DOWN/DESTROY the works of the devil) as the SOTERIOLOGICAL-PURPOSE-STATEMENT of the Incarnation. The ephanerōthē (was-manifested) is the technical-incarnational verb — the eternal-Word-who-IS becomes-visibly-manifest in flesh-and-action. The hina-purpose clause names the polemical-redemptive-telos: not abstractly 'salvation' but specifically destroying-the-works-of-the-devil — sin, death, deception, the cosmic-tyrant. Pairs with Heb 2:14 (hina dia tou thanatou katargēsē ton to kratos echonta tou thanatou, tout' estin ton diabolon — that through-death he-might-destroy the one having the power-of-death, that is, the devil) as the canonical-incarnational-destroying-the-devil pair.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Epistola ad Epictetum (c. 350 AD)

'Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God' — Athanasius marks Iēsoun Christon en sarki elēlythota (Jesus Christ in-flesh having-come) as the FOUNDATIONAL ANTI-DOCETIC CREEDAL FORMULA. The en sarki (in-flesh) is non-negotiable: the genuine-fleshly-advent of the Word excludes Docetic phantasm-Christology and Apollinarian rationalist-Christology alike. The Letter to Epictetus addresses precisely this controversy in Athanasius's own era: certain Egyptian-Christians had argued that the Word's-flesh was homoousios with the Word's-divinity (a kind of Apollinarian-reductionism in reverse). Athanasius vigorously denies this: the Word's-flesh is genuine-Mary-derived-human-flesh, NOT a divine-derivative; the Word is-from-the-Father, the flesh is-from-the-Virgin.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.59 (c. 350 AD)

'In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him' — Athanasius marks ton Huion autou ton monogenē (his ONLY-BEGOTTEN Son) as the UNIQUE-GENERATION anchor: monogenēs names the Son as uniquely-from-the-Father's-essence (monos-genos = of-one-kind / of-the-same-kind-as-the-Father-alone), distinct from any creature's-coming-into-being. The Latin tradition translates as unigenitus (only-begotten); the Greek monogenēs is more-precisely 'unique-of-his-kind.' The uniqueness excludes creature-categorization (the Son is NOT first-among-many-creatures) and the begotten-genos excludes the Spirit-pneumatomachian reduction (the Son's-generation is from-Father-essence, not creaturely-act). Pairs with Jn 1:18 (monogenēs theos — the only-begotten-God) and Jn 3:16 as the canonical monogenēs Christological-trio.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.5 (c. 350 AD)

'And we know that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding, that we may know him that is true, and we are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life' — Athanasius marks houtos estin ho alēthinos theos kai zōē aiōnios (THIS is the true God and eternal life) as the MOST EXPLICIT EXPLICIT-DEITY-OF-THE-SON Johannine-Catholic-Epistle anchor. The houtos (THIS — referring back to Jesus Christ in the immediately-preceding phrase) directly-names Christ as ho alēthinos theos (THE TRUE God, with definite article + qualifying-adjective). The Arians could not Arian-accommodate this without breaking standard Greek; Athanasius cites it as definitive against any creature-Christology.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Epistulae ad Serapionem 1.24 (c. 350 AD)

'According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue' — Athanasius marks tēs theias dynameōs autou (his divine-power) as the PNEUMATOLOGICAL EXTENSION of the 2 Pet 1:4 theōsis-grant (γ.4.9 seed anchor). The divine-power that grants life-and-godliness IS the Spirit-of-Christ; the gifts pertain to the Spirit's-economy IN-the-believer. Athanasius reads ta pros zōēn kai eusebeian (the-things-for-life-and-godliness) as the totality-of-the-Spirit's-fruits which PREPARE the believer-for-theōsis. Pairs with 2 Pet 1:4 (partakers-of-the-divine-nature) as the canonical Petrine pneumatological-theōsis pair, both grounded in the divine-power of the One who-called-us.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §54 (c. 350 AD)

'Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature' — Athanasius marks theias koinōnoi physeōs (partakers of-divine nature) as the THEOSIS-summit of the entire NT and the Petrine-anchor of his signature-formula: 'For he was made man that we might be made God' (Autos gar enēnthrōpēsen, hina hēmeis theopoiēthōmen — DI §54, the most-quoted line in all of patristic theology). The koinōnoi (partakers, sharers — strong noun, not merely 'observers' or 'imitators') names the genuine-ontological-sharing in the divine-life that the incarnation achieves for the redeemed. The theias-physeōs (divine-nature) is not creaturely-elevation (which Arian-creatures could in principle experience) but participation-in-the-essence-itself by grace. Tewahedo deification-spirituality (the Mahǝbär-Sǝmʿon ascetic tradition, the Säwasǝw-of-Pure-Thought) is built explicitly on the Athanasian-Petrine theosis-foundation.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §6 (c. 350 AD)

'The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance' — Athanasius marks mē boulomenos tinas apolesthai alla pantas eis metanoian chōrēsai (not willing any to perish but all to come to-repentance) as the DIVINE-UNIVERSAL-SALVIFIC-WILL Petrine-anchor. The divine-patience (makrothymia) is itself-incarnational: the Word's-incarnation IS the divine-patience-extended-in-time, giving humanity-time to repent. Athanasius's DI §6-7 anti-Manichaean reading of evil-as-privation-of-good rests on this universal-salvific-will: God-cannot-be-the-author-of-evil because his-will-is-toward-universal-restoration.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.46 (c. 350 AD)

'But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen' — Athanasius marks autō hē doxa nyn kai eis hēmeran aiōnos (to HIM be the glory now and unto the day of eternity) as a DOXOLOGICAL-WORSHIP-OF-CHRIST anchor that the Arians cannot consistently maintain. The doxa-directed-to-Christ is the creature's-worship-act that is owed to God-by-nature alone (the first-commandment exclusion of creature-worship). If Christ were a creature-by-nature, this doxology would be idolatrous; the verse's own-internal-logic-positively-requires Christ's-divine-essence. ↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §8 (c. 350 AD)

'But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot' — Athanasius marks haimati timiō hōs amnou amōmou kai aspilou Christou (precious blood of-Christ, as of-a-lamb without-blemish and-without-spot) as the Petrine Paschal-Christology. The amnou (lamb) connects Christ to Ex 12's-Passover-lamb (typological-fulfillment) and Jn 1:29's-Baptist-pointing (incarnational-recognition). The amōmou kai aspilou (without-blemish-and-without-spot) names the moral-sinlessness that is constitutive of the Lamb's-sufficiency for redemption. The haimati timiō (precious blood) names the value of the redemption (which only divine-blood could possess — Acts 20:28 'the church of God which he hath purchased with his own blood'). The Tewahedo Anaphora cites 1 Pet 1:19 + Jn 1:29 + Acts 20:28 as the institutional-Lamb-triad at every Eucharist.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §54 (c. 350 AD)

'Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever' — Athanasius marks dia logou zōntos theou kai menontos (through the living-and-abiding word of God) as ambiguating-favorably-toward-Christology: the divine-Logos himself effects the regeneration through whom the scriptural-logos and the Spirit-of-Christ co-act. The incorruptible-seed (sporas aphthartos) is the Word's-life-communicated; the new-birth is Christic-incorporation. Athanasius pairs 1Pe 1:23 with Jn 3:5 (water-and-Spirit re-birth) and Jas 1:18 (he-of-his-own-will brought-us-forth by-the-word-of-truth) as the canonical regeneration-by-Word-and-Spirit triplet. Theōsis-grammar requires this regeneration-prerequisite: only the new-born can be deified.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.55 (c. 350 AD)

'For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps' — Athanasius marks Christos epathen hyper hymōn (Christ suffered for us) as the SOTERIOLOGICAL-PARADIGMATIC pair: the suffering is BOTH substitutionary (hyper hymōn — on-your-behalf, in-your-place) AND paradigmatic (hypogrammon — a writing-pattern-to-copy). Christ's-suffering simultaneously redeems and exemplifies; the soteriological efficacy makes the moral-imitation possible rather than mere-moralism. The Word qua-divine cannot suffer; the Word qua-assumed-flesh genuinely-suffers and the suffering is salvifically-imputed to the Word's-Person. Pairs with 1 Pet 3:18 (Christ once-suffered for sins) as the canonical-substitutionary-Petrine-pair.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §17 (c. 350 AD)

'By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah' — Athanasius marks tois en phylakē pneumasin poreutheis ekēryxen (the spirits in prison having-gone he-preached-to-them) as the HARROWING-OF-HADES anchor: the Word's-soul (united-to-the-Word's-divinity even through the three-day-burial-pause) travels to release the OT-righteous (and to confront the OT-disobedient — the antediluvian-spirits) in the inter-mortem state. The Word does NOT release-himself from the body (the Word remains-united-to-flesh even in the tomb); rather, the unified-Christ-in-his-soul descends-to-Hades while-the-body-rests-in-the-tomb. The harrowing is the inaugural-moment of the Word's-Paschal-Cosmic-Victory. Tewahedo Holy-Saturday iconography (Anastasis-icon: Christ pulling Adam + Eve out of the tomb) preserves this 1 Peter 3:19-anchored harrowing-tradition.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Epistola ad Epictetum (c. 350 AD)

'Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh' — Athanasius marks Christou pathontos sarki (Christ-having-suffered in-flesh) as the qualifier that locates the Passion in the assumed-human-nature without compromising divine-impassibility. The Word-suffers IN the flesh he assumed (the sarki is locative, naming WHERE the suffering happens) without the divine-nature itself becoming passible. The Tewahedo Miaphysite-Christology preserves this Athanasian-distinction: the one-incarnate-Person of the Word genuinely-suffers in the flesh he-assumed, while the divine-essence remains impassible in the same-Person. The Athanasian-impassibility is NOT the denial of Christ's-human-suffering (which is real, Heb 5:8 'though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered'); it is the NATURE-distinction within the Person. The Tewahedo Holy-Friday (Sǝqlät) hymnody preserves this in its Cyrillian-Athanasian Miaphysite-confession.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Festal Letters 39 (367 AD) (c. 350 AD)

'Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning' — Athanasius marks ho Patēr tōn phōtōn par' hō ouk eni parallagē ē tropēs aposkiasma (the Father of lights, with-whom is-not variation or shadow-of-turning) as the DIVINE-IMMUTABILITY anchor. The atrepton (un-turning) and aparal-lakton (un-varying) of the Father's-essence are direct anti-Arian: the divine-Light cannot vary or turn (i.e. cannot become what-it-was-not, cannot beget-a-creature-rather-than-eternal-Word). Athanasius's inclusion of James in the NT-canon (Festal Letter 39, 367 AD) was the canonical-decision that gave the Catholic-Epistle its full-apostolic-authority in the Eastern tradition; Jas 1:17 anchors the canon-inclusion with a direct-Trinitarian-essence prooftext.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.13 (c. 350 AD)

'Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power...' — Athanasius marks the triad apaugasma tēs doxēs + charaktēr tēs hypostaseōs + pherōn ta panta as the densest Christological cluster in the NT. The apaugasma (effulgence, radiance-from-the-source) names the Son's eternal-procession-from-the-Father in the same metaphysical-mode as light-from-fire (the light is genuinely-from the fire and genuinely-of the same nature, not subordinate or temporally-later). The charaktēr tēs hypostaseōs (express-imprint of his person — the imprint that a coin shows from its die) names the perfect-ontological-imaging: the Son shows-forth precisely what the Father is. The pherōn ta panta tō rhēmati tēs dynameōs (upholding all-things by the word of his power) names the cosmic-sustaining-Christology. The Tewahedo Trisagion preserves all three Hebrews-anchor predications in its anti-Arian formula.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.55 (c. 350 AD)

'For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?' — Athanasius marks the Hebrews 1 catena-of-citations as the EARLIEST PATRISTIC-PROOFTEXT-CHAIN that the Arians could not dismantle. The author-of-Hebrews quotes Ps 2:7 + 2 Sam 7:14 + Deut 32:43 + Ps 104:4 + Ps 45:6-7 + Ps 102:25-27 + Ps 110:1 — seven OT citations applied to the Son, each excluding Arian-creature-status. The eternal-generation reading of Ps 2:7 (gegennēka se — I-have-begotten-you, perfect-tense permanent-state) is decisive: angels never receive this naming. Tewahedo Trisagion-theology cites Heb 1:5-13 + Ps 2:7 as the seven-fold-OT-Christology anchor.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.56 (c. 350 AD)

'And again, when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of God worship him' — Athanasius marks proskynēsatōsan autō pantes angeloi theou (let-worship him all angels of God) as the angelic-worship-of-Christ Hebrews-anchor. If Christ were a creature, divine-mandate to-angels-to-worship-him would be idolatry; the verse therefore-requires Christ's-divine-essence (only YHWH receives proskynēsis from angels). Athanasius pairs Heb 1:6 with Rev 5:13-14 (every-creature-worships the Lamb) as the canonical Christ-angelic-worship pair. Tewahedo Christ-Pantocrator iconography of every Tewahedo-dome preserves the Heb 1:6 + Rev 5 angelic-worship-anchor.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.61 (c. 350 AD)

'But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom' — Athanasius marks ho thronos sou ho theos (thy throne, O God) as the MOST-EXPLICIT direct-address Pauline-Hebrews-citation of the Son as ho-theos (the-God, with definite article). The Father directly-addresses the Son as 'O God' (vocative ho-theos). The Arian-reading cannot accommodate this without making it metaphorical or non-direct; Athanasian-Pauline-Hebrews exegesis takes it as literal-Trinitarian. Paired with Heb 1:9 (anointed-above-fellows, theos = the-God-anointing-by-the-God) it positively-requires intra-divine-distinction of Persons.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §10 (c. 350 AD)

'Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil' — Athanasius marks paraplēsiōs meteschen tōn autōn (likewise partook of the same) as the Pauline-anti-Docetic Hebrews-anchor. The Word-incarnate did not merely-appear-flesh-and-blood but FULLY-PARTOOK-of (meteschen) the same-substance the children possess. The hina dia tou thanatou katargēsē (that through death he might destroy) names the soteriological-purpose: only by genuinely-dying could the Word destroy death-itself. Tewahedo Christmas + Holy-Friday lectionary pairs Heb 2:14 with Phil 2:7-8 as the genuine-participation-anchor.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Epistola ad Adelphium (c. 350 AD)

'For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin' — Athanasius marks pepeirasmenon kata panta kath' homoiotēta chōris hamartias (tempted in all-things according-to-likeness without sin) as the Hebrews-formal-statement of Christ's-sinlessness-with-genuine-human-experience. The kata panta (in all-things) excludes Apollinarian-reduction (no human-aspect-missing); the kath' homoiotēta (according to likeness) excludes Docetic-non-genuineness; the chōris hamartias (without sin) excludes Adoptionist-or-Pelagian denial of Christ's-moral-perfection. Tewahedo Holy-Friday meditation cites Heb 4:15 + Rom 8:3 (homoiōmati-sarkos) as the sinless-but-tempted Pauline-Hebrews-pair.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §9 (c. 350 AD)

'How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?' — Athanasius marks dia pneumatos aiōniou heauton prosēnenken amōmon tō theō (through eternal Spirit offered himself spotless to God) as the FULL-TRINITARIAN-atonement-structure: the Son offers (active-incarnational-priest) himself (object-of-offering = the incarnate-flesh) through the eternal-Spirit (the pneumatological-medium of the sacrifice) to the Father (recipient-of-the-acceptable-offering). All three Persons are active in the single-act of atonement. Tewahedo Anaphora consecration-prayer cites Heb 9:14 at the epiclesis-of-the-Spirit-upon-the-elements as the Trinitarian-eucharistic-pattern-anchor.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). TESTAMENT occurs twelve times in the New Testament (Hebrews 9:15, etc.) as the rendering of the Gr. diatheke, which is twenty times rendered “covenant” in the Authorized Version, and always so in the Revised Version. ↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos II.10 (c. 350 AD)

'Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever' — Athanasius marks Iēsous Christos chthes kai sēmeron ho autos kai eis tous aiōnas (Jesus Christ the-same yesterday and today and unto-the-ages) as the unchangeability (atreptos) confession of the incarnate-Word. The Arian-claim that the Son is mutable (treptos, capable-of-moral-change) — a claim necessary if the Son is a creature, since creatures are by-nature changeable — is directly-contradicted by ho autos (the-same). The atreptos-Christology means: even in the incarnate-mode (where genuine-human-suffering and growth-of-wisdom Lk 2:52 occur), the eternal-Word never-altered in his divine-essence. Tewahedo Christology preserves the Athanasian-atreptos exactly: the Word in the incarnation 'remained-what-he-was and became-what-he-was-not.' Heb 13:8 + Mal 3:6 + Jas 1:17 form the canonical immutability-triad.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.41 (c. 350 AD)

'Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant' — Athanasius marks ho theos tēs eirēnēs ho anagagōn ek nekrōn ton kyrion (the God of peace who brought up from-the-dead the Lord) as the TRINITARIAN-RESURRECTION pastoral-doxology. The Father-of-peace brings up the Son through-the-blood-of-the-eternal-covenant (haimati diathēkēs aiōniou — note aiōniou, eternal, pointing to the Trinitarian-counsel before-time). The doxological-frame is what makes Hebrews's-Christology WORSHIP-able: every Christological-claim climaxes in doxology to the Father through the Son.

ONESIMUS useful, a slave who, after robbing his master Philemon (q.v.) at Colosse, fled to Rome, where he was converted by the apostle Paul, who sent him back to his master with the epistle which bears his name. In it he beseeches Philemon to receive his slave as a “faithful and beloved brother.” Paul offers to pay to Philemon anything his slave had taken, and to bear the wrong he had done him. He was accompanied on his return by Tychicus, the bearer of the Epistle to the Colossians… [Reviewer: condense Easton's entry as needed.]

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). NICOPOLIS city of victory, where Paul intended to winter (Titus 3:12). There were several cities of this name. The one here referred to was most probably that in Epirus, which was built by Augustus Caesar to commemorate his victory at the battle of Actium (B.C. 31). It is the modern Paleoprevesa, i.e., “Old Prevesa.” The subscription to the epistle to Titus calls it “Nicopolis of Macedonia”, i.e., of Thrace. This is, however, probably incorrect. [Reviewer: condense Easton's entry as needed.]

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:1.

I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, [and] giving of thanks, be made for all men;

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Παρακαλῶ οὖν πρῶτον πάντων ποιεῖσθαι δεήσεις, προσευχάς, ἐντεύξεις, εὐχαριστίας, ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀνθρώπων·

Douay-Rheims

I desire therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all men:

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Obsecro igitur primum omnium fieri obsecrationes, orationes, postulationes, gratiarum actiones, pro omnibus hominibus:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

فَأَطْلُبُ أَوَّلَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، أَنْ تُقَامَ طَلِبَاتٌ وَصَلَوَاتٌ وَٱبْتِهَالَاتٌ وَتَشَكُّرَاتٌ لِأَجْلِ جَمِيعِ ٱلنَّاسِ،

↩

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:2.

For kings, and [for] all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

ὑπὲρ βασιλέων καὶ πάντων τῶν ἐν ὑπεροχῇ ὄντων, ἵνα ἤρεμον καὶ ἡσύχιον βίον διάγωμεν ἐν πάσῃ εὐσεβείᾳ καὶ σεμνότητι.

Douay-Rheims

For kings, and for all that are in high station: that we may lead a quiet and a peaceable life in all piety and chastity.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

pro regibus, et omnibus qui in sublimitate sunt, ut quietam et tranquillam vitam agamus in omni pietate, et castitate:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَجْلِ ٱلْمُلُوكِ وَجَمِيعِ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي مَنْصِبٍ، لِكَيْ نَقْضِيَ حَيَاةً مُطْمَئِنَّةً هَادِئَةً فِي كُلِّ تَقْوَى وَوَقَارٍ،

↩

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:3.

For this [is] good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour;

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Τοῦτο γὰρ καλὸν καὶ ἀπόδεκτον ἐνώπιον τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν θεοῦ,

Douay-Rheims

For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour,

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

hoc enim bonum est, et acceptum coram Salvatore nostro Deo,

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّ هَذَا حَسَنٌ وَمَقْبُولٌ لَدَى مُخَلِّصِنَا ٱللهِ،

↩

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:4.

Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

ὃς πάντας ἀνθρώπους θέλει σωθῆναι καὶ εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας ἐλθεῖν.

Douay-Rheims

Who will have all men to be saved, and to come to the knowledge of the truth.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

qui omnes homines vult salvos fieri, et ad agnitionem veritatis venire.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

ٱلَّذِي يُرِيدُ أَنَّ جَمِيعَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَخْلُصُونَ، وَإِلَى مَعْرِفَةِ ٱلْحَقِّ يُقْبِلُونَ.

↩

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:5.

For [there is] one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Εἷς γὰρ θεός, εἷς καὶ μεσίτης θεοῦ καὶ ἀνθρώπων, ἄνθρωπος χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς,

Douay-Rheims

For there is one God, and one mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus:

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Unus enim Deus, unus et mediator Dei et hominum homo Christus Jesus:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّهُ يُوجَدُ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ وَوَسِيطٌ وَاحِدٌ بَيْنَ ٱللهِ وَٱلنَّاسِ: ٱلْإِنْسَانُ يَسُوعُ ٱلْمَسِيحُ،

↩

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:6.

Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

ὁ δοὺς ἑαυτὸν ἀντίλυτρον ὑπὲρ πάντων, τὸ μαρτύριον καιροῖς ἰδίοις,

Douay-Rheims

Who gave himself a redemption for all, a testimony in due times.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

qui dedit redemptionem semetipsum pro omnibus, testimonium temporibus suis:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

ٱلَّذِي بَذَلَ نَفْسَهُ فِدْيَةً لِأَجْلِ ٱلْجَمِيعِ، ٱلشَّهَادَةُ فِي أَوْقَاتِهَا ٱلْخَاصَّةِ،

↩

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:7.

Where unto I am ordained a preacher, and an apostle, (I speak the truth in Christ, [and] lie not;) a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

εἰς ὃ ἐτέθην ἐγὼ κῆρυξ καὶ ἀπόστολος· ἀλήθειαν λέγω ἐν χριστῷ, οὐ ψεύδομαι· διδάσκαλος ἐθνῶν ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀληθείᾳ.

Douay-Rheims

Whereunto I am appointed a preacher and an apostle, (I say the truth, I lie not,) a doctor of the Gentiles in faith and truth.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

in quo positus sum ego prædicator, et Apostolus (veritatem dico, non mentior) doctor gentium in fide, et veritate.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

ٱلَّتِي جُعِلْتُ أَنَا لَهَا كَارِزًا وَرَسُولًا. اَلْحَقَّ أَقُولُ فِي ٱلْمَسِيحِ وَلَا أَكْذِبُ، مُعَلِّمًا لِلْأُمَمِ فِي ٱلْإِيمَانِ وَٱلْحَقِّ.

↩

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:8.

I will therefore that men pray every where, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Βούλομαι οὖν προσεύχεσθαι τοὺς ἄνδρας ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ, ἐπαίροντας ὁσίους χεῖρας, χωρὶς ὀργῆς καὶ διαλογισμοῦ.

Douay-Rheims

I will therefore that men pray in every place, lifting up pure hands, without anger and contention.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Volo ergo viros orare in omni loco, levantes puras manus sine ira et disceptatione.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

فَأُرِيدُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ ٱلرِّجَالُ فِي كُلِّ مَكَانٍ، رَافِعِينَ أَيَادِيَ طَاهِرَةً، بِدُونِ غَضَبٍ وَلَا جِدَالٍ.

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:9.

In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array;

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ὡσαύτως καὶ τὰς γυναῖκας ἐν καταστολῇ κοσμίῳ, μετὰ αἰδοῦς καὶ σωφροσύνης, κοσμεῖν ἑαυτάς, μὴ ἐν πλέγμασιν, ἢ χρυσῷ, ἢ μαργαρίταις, ἢ ἱματισμῷ πολυτελεῖ,

Douay-Rheims

In like manner women also in decent apparel: adorning themselves with modesty and sobriety, not with plaited hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly attire,

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Similiter et mulieres in habitu ornato, cum verecundia et sobrietate ornantes se, et non in tortis crinibus, aut auro, aut margaritas, vel veste pretiosa:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَكَذَلِكَ أَنَّ ٱلنِّسَاءَ يُزَيِّنَّ ذَوَاتِهِنَّ بِلِبَاسِ ٱلْحِشْمَةِ، مَعَ وَرَعٍ وَتَعَقُّلٍ، لَا بِضَفَائِرَ أَوْ ذَهَبٍ أَوْ لَآلِئَ أَوْ مَلَابِسَ كَثِيرَةِ ٱلثَّمَنِ،

↩

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:10.

But (which becometh women professing godliness) with good works.

ἀλλ’ ὃ πρέπει γυναιξὶν ἐπαγγελλομέναις θεοσέβειαν, δι’ ἔργων ἀγαθῶν.

sed quod decet mulieres, promittentes pietatem per opera bona.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:11.

Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection.

Γυνὴ ἐν ἡσυχίᾳ μανθανέτω ἐν πάσῃ ὑποταγῇ.

لِتَتَعَلَّمِ ٱلْمَرْأَةُ بِسُكُوتٍ فِي كُلِّ خُضُوعٍ.

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:12.

But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.

Γυναικὶ δὲ διδάσκειν οὐκ ἐπιτρέπω, οὐδὲ αὐθεντεῖν ἀνδρός, ἀλλ’ εἶναι ἐν ἡσυχίᾳ.

Paul’s First Letter to Timothy 2:14.

And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν καὶ ταῦτα πάσχω, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐπαισχύνομαι· οἶδα γὰρ ᾧ πεπίστευκα, καὶ πέπεισμαι ὅτι δυνατός ἐστιν τὴν παραθήκην μου φυλάξαι εἰς ἐκείνην τὴν ἡμέραν.

وَٱضْطِهَادَاتِي، وَآلَامِي، مِثْلَ مَا أَصَابَنِي فِي أَنْطَاكِيَةَ وَإِيقُونِيَّةَ وَلِسْتِرَةَ. أَيَّةَ ٱضْطِهَادَاتٍ ٱحْتَمَلْتُ! وَمِنَ ٱلْجَمِيعِ أَنْقَذَنِي ٱلرَّبُّ.

Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.

وَجَمِيعُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَعِيشُوا بِٱلتَّقْوَى فِي ٱلْمَسِيحِ يَسُوعَ يُضْطَهَدُونَ.

لِكَيْ يَكُونَ إِنْسَانُ ٱللهِ كَامِلًا، مُتَأَهِّبًا لِكُلِّ عَمَلٍ صَالِحٍ.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

Καὶ σχεδὸν ἐν αἵματι πάντα καθαρίζεται κατὰ τὸν νόμον, καὶ χωρὶς αἱματεκχυσίας οὐ γίνεται ἄφεσις.

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Et omnia pene in sanguine secundum legem mundantur: et sine sanguinis effusione non fit remissio.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

فَإِنَّهُ فِي هَذَا شُهِدَ لِلْقُدَمَاءِ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:3.

Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Πίστει νοοῦμεν κατηρτίσθαι τοὺς αἰῶνας ῥήματι θεοῦ, εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐκ φαινομένων τὰ βλεπόμενα γεγονέναι.

Douay-Rheims

By faith we understand that the world was framed by the word of God; that from invisible things visible things might be made.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Fide intelligimus aptata esse sæcula verbo Dei: ut ex invisibilibus visibilia fierent.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بِٱلْإِيمَانِ نَفْهَمُ أَنَّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ أُتْقِنَتْ بِكَلِمَةِ ٱللهِ، حَتَّى لَمْ يَتَكَوَّنْ مَا يُرَى مِمَّا هُوَ ظَاهِرٌ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:4.

By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Πίστει πλείονα θυσίαν Ἄβελ παρὰ Κάϊν προσήνεγκεν τῷ θεῷ, δι’ ἧς ἐμαρτυρήθη εἶναι δίκαιος, μαρτυροῦντος ἐπὶ τοῖς δώροις αὐτοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ· καὶ δι’ αὐτῆς ἀποθανὼν ἔτι λαλεῖται.

Douay-Rheims

By faith Abel offered to God a sacrifice exceeding that of Cain, by which he obtained a testimony that he was just, God giving testimony to his gifts; and by it he being dead yet speaketh.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Fide plurimam hostiam Abel, quam Cain, obtulit Deo, per quam testimonium consecutus est esse justus, testimonium perhibente muneribus ejus Deo, et per illam defunctus adhuc loquitur.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بِٱلْإِيمَانِ قَدَّمَ هَابِيلُ لِلهِ ذَبِيحَةً أَفْضَلَ مِنْ قَايِينَ. فَبِهِ شُهِدَ لَهُ أَنَّهُ بَارٌّ، إِذْ شَهِدَ ٱللهُ لِقَرَابِينِهِ. وَبِهِ، وَإِنْ مَاتَ، يَتَكَلَّمْ بَعْدُ!

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:5.

By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Πίστει Ἐνὼχ μετετέθη τοῦ μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον, καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκετο, διότι μετέθηκεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεός· πρὸ γὰρ τῆς μεταθέσεως αὐτοῦ μεμαρτύρηται εὐηρεστηκέναι τῷ θεῷ·

Douay-Rheims

By faith Henoch was translated, that he should not see death; and he was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had testimony that he pleased God.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Fide Henoch translatus est ne videret mortem, et non inveniebatur, quia transtulit illum Deus: ante translationem enim testimonium habuit placuisse Deo.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بِٱلْإِيمَانِ نُقِلَ أَخْنُوخُ لِكَيْ لَا يَرَى ٱلْمَوْتَ، وَلَمْ يُوجَدْ لِأَنَّ ٱللهَ نَقَلَهُ. إِذْ قَبْلَ نَقْلِهِ شُهِدَ لَهُ بِأَنَّهُ قَدْ أَرْضَى ٱللهَ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:6.

But without faith [it is] impossible to please [him]: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and [that] he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

χωρὶς δὲ πίστεως ἀδύνατον εὐαρεστῆσαι· πιστεῦσαι γὰρ δεῖ τὸν προσερχόμενον τῷ θεῷ, ὅτι ἔστιν, καὶ τοῖς ἐκζητοῦσιν αὐτὸν μισθαποδότης γίνεται.

Douay-Rheims

But without faith it is impossible to please God. For he that cometh to God, must believe that he is, and is a rewarder to them that seek him.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Sine fide autem impossibile est placere Deo. Credere enim oportet accedentem ad Deum quia est, et inquirentibus se remunerator sit.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَلَكِنْ بِدُونِ إِيمَانٍ لَا يُمْكِنُ إِرْضَاؤُهُ، لِأَنَّهُ يَجِبُ أَنَّ ٱلَّذِي يَأْتِي إِلَى ٱللهِ يُؤْمِنُ بِأَنَّهُ مَوْجُودٌ، وَأَنَّهُ يُجَازِي ٱلَّذِينَ يَطْلُبُونَهُ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:7.

By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Πίστει χρηματισθεὶς Νῶε περὶ τῶν μηδέπω βλεπομένων, εὐλαβηθεὶς κατεσκεύασεν κιβωτὸν εἰς σωτηρίαν τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ· δι’ ἧς κατέκρινεν τὸν κόσμον, καὶ τῆς κατὰ πίστιν δικαιοσύνης ἐγένετο κληρονόμος.

Douay-Rheims

By faith Noe, having received an answer concerning those things which as yet were not seen, moved with fear, framed the ark for the saving of his house, by the which he condemned the world; and was instituted heir of the justice which is by faith.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Fide Noë responso accepto de iis quæ adhuc non videbantur, metuens aptavit arcam in salutem domus suæ, per quam damnavit mundum: et justitiæ, quæ per fidem est, hæres est institutus.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بِٱلْإِيمَانِ نُوحٌ لَمَّا أُوحِيَ إِلَيْهِ عَنْ أُمُورٍ لَمْ تُرَ بَعْدُ خَافَ، فَبَنَى فُلْكًا لِخَلَاصِ بَيْتِهِ، فَبِهِ دَانَ ٱلْعَالَمَ، وَصَارَ وَارِثًا لِلْبِرِّ ٱلَّذِي حَسَبَ ٱلْإِيمَانِ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:8.

By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Πίστει καλούμενος Ἀβραὰμ ὑπήκουσεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς τὸν τόπον ὃν ἤμελλεν λαμβάνειν εἰς κληρονομίαν, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν μὴ ἐπιστάμενος ποῦ ἔρχεται.

Douay-Rheims

By faith he that is called Abraham, obeyed to go out into a place which he was to receive for an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بِٱلْإِيمَانِ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لَمَّا دُعِيَ أَطَاعَ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ إِلَى ٱلْمَكَانِ ٱلَّذِي كَانَ عَتِيدًا أَنْ يَأْخُذَهُ مِيرَاثًا، فَخَرَجَ وَهُوَ لَا يَعْلَمُ إِلَى أَيْنَ يَأْتِي.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:9.

By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as [in] a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Πίστει παρῴκησεν εἰς γῆν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας, ὡς ἀλλοτρίαν, ἐν σκηναῖς κατοικήσας μετὰ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακώβ, τῶν συγκληρονόμων τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τῆς αὐτῆς·

Douay-Rheims

By faith he abode in the land, dwelling in cottages, with Isaac and Jacob, the co-heirs of the same promise.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Fide demoratus est in terra repromissionis, tamquam in aliena, in casulis habitando cum Isaac et Jacob cohæredibus repromissionis ejusdem.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:10.

Douay-Rheims

For he looked for a city that hath foundations; whose builder and maker is God.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Exspectabat enim fundamenta habentem civitatem: cujus artifex et conditor Deus.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ يَنْتَظِرُ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ ٱلَّتِي لَهَا ٱلْأَسَاسَاتُ، ٱلَّتِي صَانِعُهَا وَبَارِئُهَا ٱللهُ.

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:11.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:12.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Διὸ καὶ ἀφ’ ἑνὸς ἐγεννήθησαν, καὶ ταῦτα νενεκρωμένου, καθὼς τὰ ἄστρα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τῷ πλήθει, καὶ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος ἡ παρὰ τὸ χεῖλος τῆς θαλάσσης ἡ ἀναρίθμητος.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:16.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:17.

بِٱلْإِيمَانِ قَدَّمَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ إِسْحَاقَ وَهُوَ مُجَرَّبٌ. قَدَّمَ ٱلَّذِي قَبِلَ ٱلْمَوَاعِيدَ، وَحِيدَهُ

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:18.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:19.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بِٱلْإِيمَانِ إِسْحَاقُ بَارَكَ يَعْقُوبَ وَعِيسُو مِنْ جِهَةِ أُمُورٍ عَتِيدَةٍ.

بِٱلْإِيمَانِ يُوسُفُ عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ ذَكَرَ خُرُوجَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَأَوْصَى مِنْ جِهَةِ عِظَامِهِ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:23.

By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw [he was] a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king’s commandment.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Πίστει Μωϋσῆς γεννηθεὶς ἐκρύβη τρίμηνον ὑπὸ τῶν πατέρων αὐτοῦ, διότι εἶδον ἀστεῖον τὸ παιδίον· καὶ οὐκ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸ διάταγμα τοῦ βασιλέως.

Douay-Rheims

Arabic (Van Dyck)

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بِٱلْإِيمَانِ مُوسَى لَمَّا كَبِرَ أَبَى أَنْ يُدْعَى ٱبْنَ ٱبْنَةِ فِرْعَوْنَ،

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:25.

Douay-Rheims

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بِٱلْإِيمَانِ صَنَعَ ٱلْفِصْحَ وَرَشَّ ٱلدَّمَ لِئَلَّا يَمَسَّهُمُ ٱلَّذِي أَهْلَكَ ٱلْأَبْكَارَ.

Douay-Rheims

The Letter to the Hebrews 11:30.

Douay-Rheims

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:4.

Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Οὔπω μέχρι αἵματος ἀντικατέστητε πρὸς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἀνταγωνιζόμενοι·

Douay-Rheims

For you have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin:

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Nondum enim usque ad sanguinem restitistis, adversus peccatum repugnantes:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لَمْ تُقَاوِمُوا بَعْدُ حَتَّى ٱلدَّمِ مُجَاهِدِينَ ضِدَّ ٱلْخَطِيَّةِ،

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:5.

And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

καὶ ἐκλέλησθε τῆς παρακλήσεως, ἥτις ὑμῖν ὡς υἱοῖς διαλέγεται, Υἱέ μου, μὴ ὀλιγώρει παιδείας κυρίου, μηδὲ ἐκλύου ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐλεγχόμενος·

Douay-Rheims

And you have forgotten the consolation, which speaketh to you, as unto children, saying: My son, neglect not the discipline of the Lord; neither be thou wearied whilst thou art rebuked by him.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

et obliti estis consolationis, quæ vobis tamquam filiis loquitur, dicens: Fili mi, noli negligere disciplinam Domini: neque fatigeris dum ab eo argueris.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَقَدْ نَسِيتُمُ ٱلْوَعْظَ ٱلَّذِي يُخَاطِبُكُمْ كَبَنِينَ: «يَا ٱبْنِي، لَا تَحْتَقِرْ تَأْدِيبَ ٱلرَّبِّ، وَلَا تَخُرْ إِذَا وَبَّخَكَ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:6.

For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

ὃν γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ κύριος παιδεύει· μαστιγοῖ δὲ πάντα υἱὸν ὃν παραδέχεται.

Douay-Rheims

For whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth; and he scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Quem enim diligit Dominus, castigat: flagellat autem omnem filium, quem recipit.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّ ٱلَّذِي يُحِبُّهُ ٱلرَّبُّ يُؤَدِّبُهُ، وَيَجْلِدُ كُلَّ ٱبْنٍ يَقْبَلُهُ».

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:7.

If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Εἰς παιδείαν ὑπομένετε, ὡς υἱοῖς ὑμῖν προσφέρεται ὁ θεός· τίς γάρ ἐστιν υἱὸς ὃν οὐ παιδεύει πατήρ;

Douay-Rheims

Persevere under discipline. God dealeth with you as with his sons; for what son is there, whom the father doth not correct?

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

In disciplina perseverate. Tamquam filiis vobis offert se Deus: quis enim filius, quem non corripit pater?

Arabic (Van Dyck)

إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَحْتَمِلُونَ ٱلتَّأْدِيبَ يُعَامِلُكُمُ ٱللهُ كَٱلْبَنِينَ. فَأَيُّ ٱبْنٍ لَا يُؤَدِّبُهُ أَبُوهُ؟

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:8.

But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Εἰ δὲ χωρίς ἐστε παιδείας, ἧς μέτοχοι γεγόνασιν πάντες, ἄρα νόθοι ἐστὲ καὶ οὐχ υἱοί.

Douay-Rheims

But if you be without chastisement, whereof all are made partakers, then are you bastards, and not sons.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

quod si extra disciplinam estis, cujus participes facti sunt omnes: ergo adulteri, et non filii estis.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَلَكِنْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ بِلَا تَأْدِيبٍ، قَدْ صَارَ ٱلْجَمِيعُ شُرَكَاءَ فِيهِ، فَأَنْتُمْ نُغُولٌ لَا بَنُونَ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:9.

Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected [us], and we gave [them] reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Εἶτα τοὺς μὲν τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν πατέρας εἴχομεν παιδευτάς, καὶ ἐνετρεπόμεθα· οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑποταγησόμεθα τῷ πατρὶ τῶν πνευμάτων, καὶ ζήσομεν;

Douay-Rheims

Moreover we have had fathers of our flesh, for instructors, and we reverenced them: shall we not much more obey the Father of spirits, and live?

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Deinde patres quidem carnis nostræ, eruditores habuimus, et reverebamur eos, non multo magis obtemperabimus Patri spirituum, et vivemus?

Arabic (Van Dyck)

ثُمَّ قَدْ كَانَ لَنَا آبَاءُ أَجْسَادِنَا مُؤَدِّبِينَ، وَكُنَّا نَهَابُهُمْ. أَفَلَا نَخْضَعُ بِٱلْأَوْلَى جِدًّا لِأَبِي ٱلْأَرْوَاحِ، فَنَحْيَا؟

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:10.

For they verily for a few days chastened [us] after their own pleasure; but he for [our] profit, that [we] might be partakers of his holiness.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Οἱ μὲν γὰρ πρὸς ὀλίγας ἡμέρας κατὰ τὸ δοκοῦν αὐτοῖς ἐπαίδευον· ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ συμφέρον, εἰς τὸ μεταλαβεῖν τῆς ἁγιότητος αὐτοῦ.

Douay-Rheims

And they indeed for a few days, according to their own pleasure, instructed us: but he, for our profit, that we might receive his sanctification.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Et illi quidem in tempore paucorum dierum, secundum voluntatem suam erudiebant nos: hic autem ad id quod utile est in recipiendo sanctificationem ejus.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّ أُولَئِكَ أَدَّبُونَا أَيَّامًا قَلِيلَةً حَسَبَ ٱسْتِحْسَانِهِمْ، وَأَمَّا هَذَا فَلِأَجْلِ ٱلْمَنْفَعَةِ، لِكَيْ نَشْتَرِكَ فِي قَدَاسَتِهِ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:11.

Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Πᾶσα δὲ παιδεία πρὸς μὲν τὸ παρὸν οὐ δοκεῖ χαρᾶς εἶναι, ἀλλὰ λύπης· ὕστερον δὲ καρπὸν εἰρηνικὸν τοῖς δι’ αὐτῆς γεγυμνασμένοις ἀποδίδωσιν δικαιοσύνης.

Douay-Rheims

Now all chastisement for the present indeed seemeth not to bring with it joy, but sorrow: but afterwards it will yield, to them that are exercised by it, the most peaceable fruit of justice.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Omnis autem disciplina in præsenti quidem videtur non esse gaudii, sed mœroris: postea autem fructum pacatissimum exercitatis per eam, reddet justitiæ.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَلَكِنَّ كُلَّ تَأْدِيبٍ فِي ٱلْحَاضِرِ لَا يُرَى أَنَّهُ لِلْفَرَحِ بَلْ لِلْحَزَنِ. وَأَمَّا أَخِيرًا فَيُعْطِي ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَدَرَّبُونَ بِهِ ثَمَرَ بِرٍّ لِلسَّلَامِ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:12.

Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Διὸ τὰς παρειμένας χεῖρας καὶ τὰ παραλελυμένα γόνατα ἀνορθώσατε·

Douay-Rheims

Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees,

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Propter quod remissas manus, et soluta genua erigite,

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِذَلِكَ قَوِّمُوا ٱلْأَيَادِيَ ٱلْمُسْتَرْخِيَةَ وَٱلرُّكَبَ ٱلْمُخَلَّعَةَ،

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:13.

And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

καὶ τροχιὰς ὀρθὰς ποιήσατε τοῖς ποσὶν ὑμῶν, ἵνα μὴ τὸ χωλὸν ἐκτραπῇ, ἰαθῇ δὲ μᾶλλον.

Douay-Rheims

And make straight steps with your feet: that no one, halting, may go out of the way; but rather be healed.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

et gressus rectos facite pedibus vestris: ut non claudicans quis erret, magis autem sanetur.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَٱصْنَعُوا لِأَرْجُلِكُمْ مَسَالِكَ مُسْتَقِيمَةً، لِكَيْ لَا يَعْتَسِفَ ٱلْأَعْرَجُ، بَلْ بِٱلْحَرِيِّ يُشْفَى.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:14.

Follow peace with all [men], and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord:

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Εἰρήνην διώκετε μετὰ πάντων, καὶ τὸν ἁγιασμόν, οὗ χωρὶς οὐδεὶς ὄψεται τὸν κύριον·

Douay-Rheims

Follow peace with all men, and holiness: without which no man shall see God.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Pacem sequimini cum omnibus, et sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo videbit Deum:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

اِتْبَعُوا ٱلسَّلَامَ مَعَ ٱلْجَمِيعِ، وَٱلْقَدَاسَةَ ٱلَّتِي بِدُونِهَا لَنْ يَرَى أَحَدٌ ٱلرَّبَّ،

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:15.

Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble [you], and thereby many be defiled;

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

ἐπισκοποῦντες μή τις ὑστερῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ· μή τις ῥίζα πικρίας ἄνω φύουσα ἐνοχλῇ, καὶ διὰ ταύτης μιανθῶσιν πολλοί·

Douay-Rheims

Looking diligently, lest any man be wanting to the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up do hinder, and by it many be defiled.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

contemplantes nequis desit gratiæ Dei: ne qua radix amaritudinis sursum germinans impediat, et per illam inquinentur multi.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

مُلَاحِظِينَ لِئَلَّا يَخِيبَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ نِعْمَةِ ٱللهِ. لِئَلَّا يَطْلُعَ أَصْلُ مَرَارَةٍ وَيَصْنَعَ ٱنْزِعَاجًا، فَيَتَنَجَّسَ بِهِ كَثِيرُونَ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:16.

Lest there [be] any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

μή τις πόρνος, ἢ βέβηλος, ὡς Ἠσαῦ, ὃς ἀντὶ βρώσεως μιᾶς ἀπέδοτο τὰ πρωτοτόκια αὐτοῦ.

Douay-Rheims

Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau; who for one mess, sold his first birthright.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Ne quis fornicator, aut profanus ut Esau: qui propter unam escam vendidit primitiva sua:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ أَحَدٌ زَانِيًا أَوْ مُسْتَبِيحًا كَعِيسُو، ٱلَّذِي لِأَجْلِ أَكْلَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ بَاعَ بَكُورِيَّتَهُ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:17.

For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἴστε γὰρ ὅτι καὶ μετέπειτα, θέλων κληρονομῆσαι τὴν εὐλογίαν, ἀπεδοκιμάσθη· μετανοίας γὰρ τόπον οὐχ εὗρεν, καίπερ μετὰ δακρύων ἐκζητήσας αὐτήν.

Douay-Rheims

For know ye that afterwards, when he desired to inherit the benediction, he was rejected; for he found no place of repentance, although with tears he had sought it.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

فَإِنَّكُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ أَيْضًا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ، لَمَّا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَرِثَ ٱلْبَرَكَةَ رُفِضَ، إِذْ لَمْ يَجِدْ لِلتَّوْبَةِ مَكَانًا، مَعَ أَنَّهُ طَلَبَهَا بِدُمُوعٍ.

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:18.

For ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest,

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Οὐ γὰρ προσεληλύθατε ψηλαφωμένῳ ὄρει, καὶ κεκαυμένῳ πυρί, καὶ γνόφῳ, καὶ σκότῳ, καὶ θυέλλῃ,

Douay-Rheims

For you are not come to a mountain that might be touched, and a burning fire, and a whirlwind, and darkness, and storm,

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّكُمْ لَمْ تَأْتُوا إِلَى جَبَلٍ مَلْمُوسٍ مُضْطَرِمٍ بِٱلنَّارِ، وَإِلَى ضَبَابٍ وَظَلَامٍ وَزَوْبَعَةٍ،

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:19.

And the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which [voice] they that heard intreated that the word should not be spoken to them any more:

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

καὶ σάλπιγγος ἤχῳ, καὶ φωνῇ ῥημάτων, ἧς οἱ ἀκούσαντες παρῃτήσαντο μὴ προστεθῆναι αὐτοῖς λόγον·

Douay-Rheims

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَهُتَافِ بُوقٍ وَصَوْتِ كَلِمَاتٍ، ٱسْتَعْفَى ٱلَّذِينَ سَمِعُوهُ مِنْ أَنْ تُزَادَ لَهُمْ كَلِمَةٌ،

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:20.

(For they could not endure that which was commanded, And if so much as a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or thrust through with a dart:

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Douay-Rheims

Arabic (Van Dyck)

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:21.

καί, οὕτως φοβερὸν ἦν τὸ φανταζόμενον, Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν, Ἔκφοβός εἰμι καὶ ἔντρομος.

Douay-Rheims

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَكَانَ ٱلْمَنْظَرُ هَكَذَا مُخِيفًا حَتَّى قَالَ مُوسَى: «أَنَا مُرْتَعِبٌ وَمُرْتَعِدٌ».

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:22.

Ἀλλὰ προσεληλύθατε Σιὼν ὄρει, καὶ πόλει θεοῦ ζῶντος, Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπουρανίῳ, καὶ μυριάσιν ἀγγέλων,

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:23.

To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect,

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

πανηγύρει καὶ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρωτοτόκων ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἀπογεγραμμένων, καὶ κριτῇ θεῷ πάντων, καὶ πνεύμασιν δικαίων τετελειωμένων,

وَكَنِيسَةُ أَبْكَارٍ مَكْتُوبِينَ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ، وَإِلَى ٱللهِ دَيَّانِ ٱلْجَمِيعِ، وَإِلَى أَرْوَاحِ أَبْرَارٍ مُكَمَّلِينَ،

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:24.

And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than [that of] Abel.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

καὶ διαθήκης νέας μεσίτῃ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ αἵματι ῥαντισμοῦ κρεῖττον λαλοῦντι παρὰ τὸν Ἄβελ.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:25.

See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more [shall not] we [escape], if we turn away from him that [speaketh] from heaven:

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Βλέπετε μὴ παραιτήσησθε τὸν λαλοῦντα. Εἰ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι οὐκ ἔφυγον, τὸν ἐπὶ γῆς παραιτησάμενοι χρηματίζοντα, πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς οἱ τὸν ἀπ’ οὐρανῶν ἀποστρεφόμενοι·

Arabic (Van Dyck)

اُنْظُرُوا أَنْ لَا تَسْتَعْفُوا مِنَ ٱلْمُتَكَلِّمِ. لِأَنَّهُ إِنْ كَانَ أُولَئِكَ لَمْ يَنْجُوا إِذِ ٱسْتَعْفَوْا مِنَ ٱلْمُتَكَلِّمِ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ، فَبِٱلْأَوْلَى جِدًّا لَا نَنْجُو نَحْنُ ٱلْمُرْتَدِّينَ عَنِ ٱلَّذِي مِنَ ٱلسَّمَاءِ!

↩

The Letter to the Hebrews 12:26.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Douay-Rheims

ita ut confidenter dicamus: Dominus mihi adjutor: non timebo quid faciat mihi homo.

كُلُّ عَطِيَّةٍ صَالِحَةٍ وَكُلُّ مَوْهِبَةٍ تَامَّةٍ هِيَ مِنْ فَوْقُ، نَازِلَةٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ أَبِي ٱلْأَنْوَارِ، ٱلَّذِي لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ تَغْيِيرٌ وَلَا ظِلُّ دَوَرَانٍ.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Sic loquimini, et sic facite sicut per legem libertatis incipientes judicari.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

هَكَذَا تَكَلَّمُوا وَهَكَذَا ٱفْعَلُوا كَعَتِيدِينَ أَنْ تُحَاكَمُوا بِنَامُوسِ ٱلْحُرِّيَّةِ.

↩

The Letter from James 2:13.

For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّ ٱلْحُكْمَ هُوَ بِلَا رَحْمَةٍ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَعْمَلْ رَحْمَةً، وَٱلرَّحْمَةُ تَفْتَخِرُ عَلَى ٱلْحُكْمِ.

↩

The Letter from James 2:14.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Douay-Rheims

What shall it profit, my brethren, if a man say he hath faith, but hath not works? Shall faith be able to save him?

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

مَا ٱلْمَنْفَعَةُ يَا إِخْوَتِي إِنْ قَالَ أَحَدٌ إِنَّ لَهُ إِيمَانًا وَلَكِنْ لَيْسَ لَهُ أَعْمَالٌ، هَلْ يَقْدِرُ ٱلْإِيمَانُ أَنْ يُخَلِّصَهُ؟

The Letter from James 2:15.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

إِنْ كَانَ أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ عُرْيَانَيْنِ وَمُعْتَازَيْنِ لِلْقُوتِ ٱلْيَوْمِيِّ،

↩

The Letter from James 2:16.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

εἴπῃ δέ τις αὐτοῖς ἐξ ὑμῶν, Ὑπάγετε ἐν εἰρήνῃ, θερμαίνεσθε καὶ χορτάζεσθε, μὴ δῶτε δὲ αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐπιτήδεια τοῦ σώματος, τί τὸ ὄφελος;

dicat autem aliquis ex vobis illis: Ite in pace, calefacimini et saturamini: non dederitis autem eis quæ necessaria sunt corpori, quid proderit?

Arabic (Van Dyck)

فَقَالَ لَهُمَا أَحَدُكُمُ: «ٱمْضِيَا بِسَلَامٍ، ٱسْتَدْفِئَا وَٱشْبَعَا»، وَلَكِنْ لَمْ تُعْطُوهُمَا حَاجَاتِ ٱلْجَسَدِ، فَمَا ٱلْمَنْفَعَةُ؟

The Letter from James 2:17.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Sic et fides, si non habeat opera, mortua est in semetipsa.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

هَكَذَا ٱلْإِيمَانُ أَيْضًا، إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ أَعْمَالٌ، مَيِّتٌ فِي ذَاتِهِ.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἀλλ’ ἐρεῖ τις, Σὺ πίστιν ἔχεις, κἀγὼ ἔργα ἔχω· δεῖξόν μοι τὴν πίστιν σου ἐκ τῶν ἔργων σου, κἀγὼ δείξω σοι ἐκ τῶν ἔργων μου τὴν πίστιν μου.

Douay-Rheims

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لَكِنْ يَقُولُ قَائِلٌ: «أَنْتَ لَكَ إِيمَانٌ، وَأَنَا لِي أَعْمَالٌ. أَرِنِي إِيمَانَكَ بِدُونِ أَعْمَالِكَ، وَأَنَا أُرِيكَ بِأَعْمَالِي إِيمَانِي».

↩

The Letter from James 2:19.

Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.

Douay-Rheims

Thou believest that there is one God. Thou dost well: the devils also believe and tremble.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Tu credis quoniam unus est Deus: bene facis: et dæmones credunt, et contremiscunt.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

أَنْتَ تُؤْمِنُ أَنَّ ٱللهَ وَاحِدٌ. حَسَنًا تَفْعَلُ. وَٱلشَّيَاطِينُ يُؤْمِنُونَ وَيَقْشَعِرُّونَ!

The Letter from James 2:20.

Vis autem scire, o homo inanis, quoniam fides sine operibus mortua est?

Arabic (Van Dyck)

The Letter from James 2:21.

linguam autem nullus hominum domare potest: inquietum malum, plena veneno mortifero.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَأَمَّا ٱللِّسَانُ، فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَحَدٌ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ أَنْ يُذَلِّلَهُ. هُوَ شَرٌّ لَا يُضْبَطُ، مَمْلُوٌّ سُمًّا مُمِيتًا.

↩

The Letter from James 3:9.

Therewith bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the similitude of God.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἐν αὐτῇ εὐλογοῦμεν τὸν θεὸν καὶ πατέρα, καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ καταρώμεθα τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς καθ’ ὁμοίωσιν θεοῦ γεγονότας·

Douay-Rheims

By it we bless God and the Father: and by it we curse men, who are made after the likeness of God.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

In ipsa benedicimus Deum et Patrem: et in ipsa maledicimus homines, qui ad similitudinem Dei facti sunt.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بِهِ نُبَارِكُ ٱللهَ ٱلْآبَ، وَبِهِ نَلْعَنُ ٱلنَّاسَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَدْ تَكَوَّنُوا عَلَى شِبْهِ ٱللهِ.

↩

The Letter from James 3:10.

Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ στόματος ἐξέρχεται εὐλογία καὶ κατάρα. Οὐ χρή, ἀδελφοί μου, ταῦτα οὕτως γίνεσθαι.

Douay-Rheims

Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Ex ipso ore procedit benedictio et maledictio. Non oportet, fratres mei, hæc ita fieri.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

مِنَ ٱلْفَمِ ٱلْوَاحِدِ تَخْرُجُ بَرَكَةٌ وَلَعْنَةٌ! لَا يَصْلُحُ يَا إِخْوَتِي أَنْ تَكُونَ هَذِهِ ٱلْأُمُورُ هَكَذَا!

↩

The Letter from James 3:11.

Doth a fountain send forth at the same place sweet [water] and bitter?

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Μήτι ἡ πηγὴ ἐκ τῆς αὐτῆς ὀπῆς βρύει τὸ γλυκὺ καὶ τὸ πικρόν;

Douay-Rheims

Doth a fountain send forth, out of the same hole, sweet and bitter water?

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Numquid fons de eodem foramine emanat dulcem et amaram aquam?

Arabic (Van Dyck)

أَلَعَلَّ يَنْبُوعًا يُنْبِعُ مِنْ نَفْسِ عَيْنٍ وَاحِدَةٍ ٱلْعَذْبَ وَٱلْمُرَّ؟

↩

The Letter from James 3:12.

Can the fig tree, my brethren, bear olive berries? either a vine, figs? so [can] no fountain both yield salt water and fresh.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Μὴ δύναται, ἀδελφοί μου, συκῆ ἐλαίας ποιῆσαι, ἢ ἄμπελος σῦκα; Οὕτως οὐδεμία πηγὴ ἁλυκὸν καὶ γλυκὺ ποιῆσαι ὕδωρ.

Douay-Rheims

Can the fig tree, my brethren, bear grapes; or the vine, figs? So neither can the salt water yield sweet.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Numquid potest, fratres mei, ficus uvas facere, aut vitis ficus? Sic neque salsa dulcem potest facere aquam.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

هَلْ تَقْدِرُ يَا إِخْوَتِي تِينَةٌ أَنْ تَصْنَعَ زَيْتُونًا، أَوْ كَرْمَةٌ تِينًا؟ وَلَا كَذَلِكَ يَنْبُوعٌ يَصْنَعُ مَاءً مَالِحًا وَعَذْبًا!

↩

The Letter from James 3:13.

Who [is] a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Τίς σοφὸς καὶ ἐπιστήμων ἐν ὑμῖν; Δειξάτω ἐκ τῆς καλῆς ἀναστροφῆς τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἐν πρᾳΰτητι σοφίας.

Douay-Rheims

Who is a wise man, and endued with knowledge among you? Let him shew, by a good conversation, his work in the meekness of wisdom.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Quis sapiens et disciplinatus inter vos? Ostendat ex bona conversatione operationem suam in mansuetudine sapientiæ.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

مَنْ هُوَ حَكِيمٌ وَعَالِمٌ بَيْنَكُمْ، فَلْيُرِ أَعْمَالَهُ بِٱلتَّصَرُّفِ ٱلْحَسَنِ فِي وَدَاعَةِ ٱلْحِكْمَةِ.

↩

The Letter from James 3:14.

But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Εἰ δὲ ζῆλον πικρὸν ἔχετε καὶ ἐριθείαν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν, μὴ κατακαυχᾶσθε καὶ ψεύδεσθε κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας.

Douay-Rheims

But if you have bitter zeal, and there be contentions in your hearts; glory not, and be not liars against the truth.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Quod si zelum amarum habetis, et contentiones sint in cordibus vestris: nolite gloriari, et mendaces esse adversus veritatem:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَلَكِنْ إِنْ كَانَ لَكُمْ غَيْرَةٌ مُرَّةٌ وَتَحَزُّبٌ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ، فَلَا تَفْتَخِرُوا وَتَكْذِبُوا عَلَى ٱلْحَقِّ.

↩

The Letter from James 3:15.

This wisdom descendeth not from above, but [is] earthly, sensual, devilish.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Οὐκ ἔστιν αὕτη ἡ σοφία ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη, ἀλλ’ ἐπίγειος, ψυχική, δαιμονιώδης.

Douay-Rheims

For this is not wisdom, descending from above: but earthly, sensual, devilish.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

non est enim ista sapientia desursum descendens: sed terrena, animalis, diabolica.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لَيْسَتْ هَذِهِ ٱلْحِكْمَةُ نَازِلَةً مِنْ فَوْقُ، بَلْ هِيَ أَرْضِيَّةٌ نَفْسَانِيَّةٌ شَيْطَانِيَّةٌ.

↩

The Letter from James 3:16.

For where envying and strife [is], there [is] confusion and every evil work.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ὅπου γὰρ ζῆλος καὶ ἐριθεία, ἐκεῖ ἀκαταστασία καὶ πᾶν φαῦλον πρᾶγμα.

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Ubi enim zelus et contentio, ibi inconstantia et omne opus pravum.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّهُ حَيْثُ ٱلْغَيْرَةُ وَٱلتَّحَزُّبُ، هُنَاكَ ٱلتَّشْوِيشُ وَكُلُّ أَمْرٍ رَدِيءٍ.

↩

The Letter from James 3:17.

But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, [and] easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἡ δὲ ἄνωθεν σοφία πρῶτον μὲν ἁγνή ἐστιν, ἔπειτα εἰρηνική, ἐπιεικής, εὐπειθής, μεστὴ ἐλέους καὶ καρπῶν ἀγαθῶν, ἀδιάκριτος καὶ ἀνυπόκριτος.

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Quæ autem desursum est sapientia, primum quidem pudica est, deinde pacifica, modesta, suadibilis, bonus consentiens, plena misericordia et fructibus bonis, non judicans, sine simulatione.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَأَمَّا ٱلْحِكْمَةُ ٱلَّتِي مِنْ فَوْقُ فَهِيَ أَوَّلًا طَاهِرَةٌ، ثُمَّ مُسَالِمَةٌ، مُتَرَفِّقَةٌ، مُذْعِنَةٌ، مَمْلُوَّةٌ رَحْمَةً وَأَثْمَارًا صَالِحَةً، عَدِيمَةُ ٱلرَّيْبِ وَٱلرِّيَاءِ.

↩

The Letter from James 3:18.

And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Καρπὸς δὲ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἐν εἰρήνῃ σπείρεται τοῖς ποιοῦσιν εἰρήνην.

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Fructus autem justitiæ, in pace seminatur, facientibus pacem.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَثَمَرُ ٱلْبِرِّ يُزْرَعُ فِي ٱلسَّلَامِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْعَلُونَ ٱلسَّلَامَ.

↩

The Letter from James 4:1.

From whence [come] wars and fightings among you? [come they] not hence, [even] of your lusts that war in your members?

Πόθεν πόλεμοι καὶ μάχαι ἐν ὑμῖν; Οὐκ ἐντεῦθεν, ἐκ τῶν ἡδονῶν ὑμῶν τῶν στρατευομένων ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ὑμῶν;

Arabic (Van Dyck)

مِنْ أَيْنَ ٱلْحُرُوبُ وَٱلْخُصُومَاتُ بَيْنَكُمْ؟ أَلَيْسَتْ مِنْ هُنَا: مِنْ لَذَّاتِكُمُ ٱلْمُحَارِبَةِ فِي أَعْضَائِكُمْ؟

The Letter from James 4:2.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἐπιθυμεῖτε, καὶ οὐκ ἔχετε· φονεύετε καὶ ζηλοῦτε, καὶ οὐ δύνασθε ἐπιτυχεῖν· μάχεσθε καὶ πολεμεῖτε, οὐκ ἔχετε διὰ τὸ μὴ αἰτεῖσθαι ὑμᾶς·

Douay-Rheims

concupiscitis, et non habetis: occiditis, et zelatis: et non potestis adipisci: litigatis, et belligeratis, et non habetis, propter quod non postulatis.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

تَشْتَهُونَ وَلَسْتُمْ تَمْتَلِكُونَ. تَقْتُلُونَ وَتَحْسِدُونَ وَلَسْتُمْ تَقْدِرُونَ أَنْ تَنَالُوا. تُخَاصِمُونَ وَتُحَارِبُونَ وَلَسْتُمْ تَمْتَلِكُونَ، لِأَنَّكُمْ لَا تَطْلُبُونَ.

↩

The Letter from James 4:3.

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

تَطْلُبُونَ وَلَسْتُمْ تَأْخُذُونَ، لِأَنَّكُمْ تَطْلُبُونَ رَدِيًّا لِكَيْ تُنْفِقُوا فِي لَذَّاتِكُمْ.

Μοιχοὶ καὶ μοιχαλίδες, οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἡ φιλία τοῦ κόσμου ἔχθρα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστίν; Ὃς ἂν οὖν βουληθῇ φίλος εἶναι τοῦ κόσμου, ἐχθρὸς τοῦ θεοῦ καθίσταται.

أَيُّهَا ٱلزُّنَاةُ وَٱلزَّوَانِي، أَمَا تَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ ٱلْعَالَمِ عَدَاوَةٌ لِلهِ؟ فَمَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُحِبًّا لِلْعَالَمِ، فَقَدْ صَارَ عَدُوًّا لِلهِ.

↩

↩

↩

The Letter from James 4:11.

Μὴ καταλαλεῖτε ἀλλήλων, ἀδελφοί. Ὁ καταλαλῶν ἀδελφοῦ, καὶ κρίνων τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καταλαλεῖ νόμου, καὶ κρίνει νόμον· εἰ δὲ νόμον κρίνεις, οὐκ εἶ ποιητὴς νόμου, ἀλλὰ κριτής.

The Letter from James 4:12.

qui ignoratis quid erit in crastino.

ٱلْأَمْرُ ٱلَّذِي فِيهِ يَسْتَغْرِبُونَ أَنَّكُمْ لَسْتُمْ تَرْكُضُونَ مَعَهُمْ إِلَى فَيْضِ هَذِهِ ٱلْخَلَاعَةِ عَيْنِهَا، مُجَدِّفِينَ.
